extracted.intended_audience: patent appellants and patent practitioners (attorneys/agents) handling PTAB ex parte appeals
extracted.subtask_description: Practical and procedural guidance on how an appellant should respond when an examiner’s answer in a PTAB ex parte appeal contains a new ground of rejection (designated or undesignated), including available filings, timing, and consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner may include a new ground of rejection (rule authority)
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner’s answer may include a new ground of rejection under 37 C.F.R. § 41.39(a)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule requires Director approval for any new ground in an examiner’s answer; see MPEP § 1207.03(I). New grounds must be prominently identified with a subheading “New Grounds of Rejection.”

rubrics_metrics.name: What constitutes a 'new ground of rejection'
rubrics_metrics.description: A rejection is a new ground if evidence (e.g., a new prior art reference) is applied or cited for the first time in the examiner’s answer, or if the examiner’s position/rationale changes the 'basic thrust of the rejection.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether a change is a new ground is highly fact-specific (Final Rule, 76 Fed. Reg. 72270, 72276; In re Kronig). The Final Rule gives case-based examples to determine when the thrust has changed.

rubrics_metrics.name: When examiner designates an answer as containing a new ground (approved by Director): two response options
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner designates a new ground of rejection and obtains Technology Center Director approval, the appellant must, within two months from the examiner’s answer, either (1) request to withdraw the appeal and reopen prosecution by filing a reply under 37 C.F.R. § 1.111, or (2) request to maintain the appeal by filing a reply brief under 37 C.F.R. § 41.41 that addresses each new ground.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the appellant fails to choose one of these options within two months, the PTAB will dismiss the appeal as to the claims subject to the new ground of rejection. See 37 C.F.R. § 41.39(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on submitting amendments/evidence with a Reply Brief to address a designated new ground
rubrics_metrics.description: An appellant may not submit any amendment, affidavit, or other evidence along with a Reply Brief under 37 C.F.R. § 41.41 in response to a new ground of rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Reply Brief accompanied by an amendment, affidavit, or other evidence will be treated as a request to reopen prosecution (i.e., as if filed under § 1.111). See 37 C.F.R. § 41.39(b)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: If examiner’s answer contains an undesignated new ground: two options
rubrics_metrics.description: When the examiner’s answer contains findings, reasoning, or explanations that differ from the Office action and may constitute an undesignated new ground, the appellant may either (1) file a reply brief under 37 C.F.R. § 41.41 to maintain the appeal and present responsive arguments, or (2) file a petition to the Director under 37 C.F.R. § 1.181 seeking review of the examiner’s failure to designate the rejection as a new ground.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing a petition puts the appeal on hold and routes the petition to a Technology Center Director for decision (see 37 C.F.R. § 41.40(a) and MPEP § 1002.02(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper use and consequences of a petition under 37 C.F.R. § 1.181
rubrics_metrics.description: An appellant should file a petition to the Director under § 1.181 only if the appellant wishes to reopen prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the petition is granted, the appellant must file a reply under § 1.111 to reopen prosecution; failure to do so will result in dismissal. The petition tolls the time for filing a reply brief (§ 41.40(a)), so an appellant should not file a reply brief the same day as the petition. If the petition is denied, the appellant will have two months to file a reply brief under § 41.41. Filing a reply brief before the petition decision is treated as a request to withdraw the petition and to maintain the appeal (37 C.F.R. § 41.40(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing: two-month deadline for responses to examiner’s answer
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a two-month time limit from the date of the examiner’s answer for the appellant to choose among the procedural options (withdraw and reopen prosecution or maintain the appeal by filing a reply brief) when a new ground has been designated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a petition under § 1.181 is filed, the time period is tolled until the petition is decided; if petition denied, two-month period to file reply begins (37 C.F.R. §§ 41.39(b), 41.40(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of inaction when facing an undesignated new ground
rubrics_metrics.description: If an appellant takes no action after an examiner’s answer that the appellant believes contains an undesignated new ground, the appellant risks waiver and other adverse consequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to timely file a petition under § 1.181 is a waiver of any arguments that the rejection must be designated as a new ground (37 C.F.R. § 41.40(a)). Also, failing to file a reply brief under § 41.41 means the PTAB panel may be persuaded by the examiner’s statements without benefit of an appellant’s rebuttal. Proceeding to PTAB without timely responsive filings may have adverse effects on the appeal outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing interplay: reply brief vs. petition timing and effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing a reply brief while a § 1.181 petition is pending has specific consequences and is treated as withdrawing the petition and maintaining the appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not file a reply brief the same day as a petition because the petition tolls the reply deadline. If a reply brief is filed prior to resolution of the petition, the Office treats it as withdrawing the petition and maintaining the appeal (37 C.F.R. § 41.40(d)).
